newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UK will reserve judgment on EMU budget pact - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: UK will reserve judgment on EMU budget pact - Clarke.

text.p: Britain will reserve judgment on a budget disciplinary pact under a common European currency should an accord be reached on Monday among EU finance ministers, Kenneth Clarke, Chancellor of the Exchequer said.
"I will put in a parliamentary scrutiny reserve if any political agreement is reached," Clarke told reporters ahead of the meeting.
EU finance ministers are meeting to consider a so-called stability pact for countries inside a future monetary union, as well as other issues pertaining to the single currency.
Clarke said any agreement would have to be finalised next June in Amsterdam at a summit of EU leaders.
He added that differences among the 15-nation bloc over the nuts and bolts of the budget pact were mostly of "emphasis."
"We are more flexible I think than the Germans might be inclined to be," Clarke said.
Tough German demands over the details of the pact have held up a final agreement among EU finance ministers.
